convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load the external 'InverseReaction' custom indicator which is not a built-in MT5 indicator. The signal logic depends entirely on this custom indicator's two buffers (IRC and IRL), requiring the indicator's calculation logic to be replicated or ported for Python conversion.

derived_values.name: mincriteria - minimum signal threshold in price units
maxcriteria - maximum signal threshold in price units

other_exits: SL/TP only - no signal-based exit; positions are managed entirely by fixed SL/TP

custom_logic_notes: Signal logic: On each new bar (using bar[1] and bar[2] from indicator buffers), the EA computes the absolute value of IRC (change) and compares it against IRL (inverse reaction level). A valid signal requires: (1) change > IRL for at least bar[1], (2) change is between mincriteria and maxcriteria, (3) exactly one of the two checked bars satisfies the criteria (not both). Direction: if IRC[0]<0 → buy (inverse reaction corrects a negative unusual impact upward); if IRC[0]>=0 → sell (inverse reaction corrects a positive unusual impact downward). The 'only one bar triggers' rule (sign[0]!=0 && sign[0]+sign[1]!=2) acts as a freshness/impulse filter ensuring the signal is new and not persistent.
python_conversion_notes: The custom InverseReaction indicator must be reverse-engineered or reimplemented in Python. It has two buffers: buffer 0 (IRC) = price change weighted by a moving average and coefficient, buffer 1 (IRL) = threshold level. The entry logic uses previous completed bars (shift=1 for both buffers, copying 2 values) so on-bar processing is straightforward. SL/TP are in raw points (StopLoss*Point, TakeProfit*Point) - be careful with pip vs point conversion for 5-digit brokers. The 'single-bar freshness' filter (sign[0] true but not sign[1]) is unique and must be preserved. No digit adjustment is performed by the EA itself.
